title: On the road with the Greyhound-sponsored band
summary: He spent a summer on one-nighters through the South with Frank Silverhead's band, with an all-New Orleans lineup.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I went on the road there one year with Frank Silverhead, the head of band one time. And we played in more bonds and tobacco bonds and things all around Georgia and South Carolina and Tennessee and Florida, all the southern states, you know. We went as far as South Carolina. The band was sponsored by the Tesh Greyhound Company. And they finished the transportation and naturally we called it a band, the Tesh Greyhound Band, you know. And we played all around, all southern Louisiana, all Lafayette and Lake Charles, all that section, and then moved up. Spent the whole summer on the road, one-nighters.
Were they mostly New Orleans guys?

All New Orleans. All New Orleans colors. Al Belanco played trumpet and Earl Danton, saxophone, I played alto, lead alto and who was it? Tony Costa I believe played tenor. And Johnny Castang played drums. Frank Federico, and later we ended up with Louis Prima for quite a while. Federico and Castang, myself. Played with Louis quite a while here. Before Louis gave the band up to go to New York, then I took over the band.
